newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says not part of any deal on Italy EMU timing.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says not part of any deal on Italy EMU timing.

text.p: Germany is not part of any European deal on the timing of Italy's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU), a Finance MInistry spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

"There are no such plans with German participation," she said, responding to a report in the Financial Times that European Union officials were concocting a face-saving deal that would allow Italy to enter EMU in 2000 or 2001, but not at the 1999 start.
The decision on which countries will participate in EMU will not be made until early 1998, on the basis of the criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty, the Finance Ministry spokeswoman said.
But even countries joining later will have to fulfil the criteria, she said.
Italy has said it is committed to joining EMU at the start, but many German and other officials have said its participation could weaken the future single currency.
